faqs.q: What does a band cost for a corporate event in Denver?
faqs.a: Our published rates run from $1,050 for a one-hour duo up to $18,000 for a thirteen-piece over four hours. Most corporate parties land between $6,000 and $12,500. Sound, lighting and an engineer are included at every size. Travel outside the metro and holiday weekends are quoted as separate lines, never folded into the total.

Two parts. A call-out covers the evening we commit regardless of length — travel, load-in, setup, sound check, strike and production. Then an hourly rate for performance time. That means a one-hour booking is priced honestly rather than forced into a four-hour block, and there is no overtime rate: hour five costs what hour four cost.

faqs.q: Do you provide a certificate of insurance?
faqs.a: Yes, naming your venue as additional insured, sent with the contract rather than after you ask. A W-9 and an itemised invoice come with it.

faqs.q: Can one booking cover cocktails and dancing?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is cheaper than two vendors. Once we are in the building the call-out is already paid, so adding a smaller group for ceremony, cocktails or dinner bills at the hourly rate only. An hour of cocktail duo added to a full band booking is $450.

faqs.q: Who do we deal with on the night?
faqs.a: One named person, given to you before the event and reachable throughout it — usually one of the players, most often the bandleader. You are never hunting for whoever looks in charge. That is included in every booking and is not an add-on.

faqs.q: How far in advance should we book?
faqs.a: Corporate holiday parties are typically decided August through October for November and December. Weddings and galas run longer — ten to twelve months, and twelve to eighteen for a mountain venue or a fall Saturday.
